args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1, the service failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of about 18%. The release candidate v2.3.1-rc was also marked unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Checked after the rollback: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and look at why v2.3.1 was promoted even though the RC was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again.

- **Which version I picked:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1, the latest deploy, is marked unhealthy. There's also a v2.3.1-rc, but it only ran in staging, where it was also unhealthy, so it didn't count.
- **Rollback:** us-east, us-west and eu-west all moved from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0. When I checked again afterwards, the service was healthy and the error rate had dropped from 18% to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the check afterwards. It also lists two follow-ups: find the root cause before v2.3.1 is redeployed, and figure out why v2.3.1 went to production even though its release candidate was unhealthy in staging.

content.text: The most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1 is unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was staging-only). Rolling back.
